$comment:
The cockpit scheduler's jobs: kind 'script' = run `cmd` (an argv array, no shell; a relative cmd[0] such as .venv/Scripts/python.exe resolves against the FUND ROOT) with cwd = `cwd` (fund-relative), killed at timeout_s; `cadence` is LOCAL time, one of 'daily HH:MM' | 'every Nh' | 'every Nm' | 'weekly DOW HH:MM' | 'at <iso>', an occurrence not started within window_s is logged missed.
`health: true` = the scheduler records the job's reading (ops.health_readings system:<id>) from the exit code (0 ok, 1 fail, else unknown; a job's own `exit` map, e.g. {"1": "unknown"}, overrides a code, never a kill); false = the tool records its own reading(s) and the scheduler must not add one. Fields may be added; never rename id/kind/cadence/cwd/cmd/window_s/timeout_s/health.

jobs.note: every probe, one subprocess each (it writes its own probe-sweep row)
jobs.why: The one writer of the probe rows. One subprocess per probe, so a hung call costs exactly one row.

jobs.note: uncommitted and unpushed work in every repo of repos.json
jobs.why: Only `behind > 0` is unconditionally red; the dirty/ahead limits are wide on purpose, because a probe that reddens at a normal day's in-flight work gets ignored.

jobs.note: silence -> a red row. The job that notices the others stopped
jobs.why: It walks the probe REGISTRY, not the health directory, so a probe whose file was never written renders `unknown - never reported`. It writes no row of its own, so it takes the scheduler's.

jobs.note: the retro debt line over every lab/ desk - due at 7 days or 5 runs
jobs.why: The mechanism behind the retro nag: it reads each desk's stamp, counts the pre-registered runs since it, and answers in an exit code (1 = a desk is due). A due retro is a nag, not a failure, so exit 1 reads as unknown (amber), never a red fail.

jobs.note: calibration per lab/ desk; flags a judge predicting too wide
jobs.why: A band that always hits is not a good judge, it is a wide one, and nobody writes that flag by hand. Exit 0 always: a report, not a gate.

jobs.note: tokens per agent (the roster, app/agents/<id>.md) per day -> its reading system:budget in the ops store
jobs.why: The moment an unattended loop can spend without a ceiling, a bug in a cadence becomes a bill. The meter reads Claude Code's own session transcripts.

jobs.note: the week, per agent per day, for the retro
jobs.why: `--no-health` on purpose: the daily `budget` job owns the system:budget reading, and a weekly window written into a daily row would date the wall wrong.

jobs.note: pg_dump of the ops store, checked with pg_restore --list, newest 14 kept (database's fund_db.backup)
jobs.why: The ops store (PostgreSQL, through @fund/db) holds every conversation, job run and usage row; a nightly ops-YYYY-MM-DD.dump under ~/fund-data/backups/db keeps 14 days to restore from.

jobs.note: the self-improvement loop: metrics, lessons, proposals, watches
jobs.why: One pass a day: rebuild the per-agent score series, capture lessons, propose, and close or revert watched changes.

jobs.note: done board items older than 14 days move to board/done/, committed
jobs.why: The Board room reads board/*.md only, so a done column that only grows buries the live work. The archive keeps the highest-numbered item (ids are max+1 of board/), anything a staying item names in blocked_by, and anything uncommitted; it commits exactly the moved paths (Agent: fund, Board-Archive trailer) and never pushes. Exit 1 = refused commit, every file put back.

jobs.note: the market cache: evict every month nobody read in 14 days, then down to the 500 MB budget; reports the cache, pins and archive sizes
jobs.why: B-0322 / B-0335 (the owner, 2026-10-03: "set up like a weekly data cleaning loop"). The CACHE class is rebuildable by design, so cleaning it loses nothing; the command never touches a pin or an archive series (database: a test pins a series, ages its cache month, cleans and reads the pin back). Exit 0 = ok (a run that evicted nothing too), 1 = it could not run OR the cache is still over budget after the clean (only archive or locked months remain: a human must look). The last stdout line is one JSON object; archive_bytes growing week on week is the number the owner asked to see, and the Data room shows it. Sunday 05:30 sits after board-archive (05:00). Grace 24h: the scheduler runs only while fundd is up and never runs late.
